mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which can stimulate economic growth and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are not higher than the baseline during periods when FEDFUNDS is low, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in the unemployment rate suggests a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are negative when the unemployment rate is below 5%, this hypothesis is disproven.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong demand in the housing market, which can lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts increase but S&P 500 returns are negative, this hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production suggests increased economic output, which can lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production increases but S&P 500 returns are negative, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales indicates strong consumer demand, which can lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If retail sales increase but S&P 500 returns are negative, this hypothesis is disproven.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate may indicate tighter monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If the federal funds rate rises above 2% but S&P 500 returns are positive, this hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate alongside an increase in payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, which can lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If both the unemployment rate decreases and payroll employment increases but S&P 500 returns are negative, this hypothesis is disproven.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates economic growth, which can lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP increases but S&P 500 returns are negative, this hypothesis is invalidated.
